content: A burning sensation, cramping pain, rectal irritation, and tenesmus may occur with the use of this product. Severe gastrointestinal obstruction or impaction can also result. This product should not be used if abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting are present unless specifically directed by a physician. Frequent or prolonged use of laxatives may lead to dependency. If rectal bleeding occurs or there is a failure to have a bowel movement, medical attention is required. Consult a physician before use if there is a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks. Do not use this product for longer than one week. If constipation persists after one week of use, contact your physician. If no bowel movement occurs within one hour of using this product, seek medical advice. Keep this product out of the reach of children. If swallowed accidentally, seek immediate medical help or contact a poison control center. Regarding pregnancy, there is no available data on its safety. For lactation, its compatibility with breastfeeding is unknown but likely acceptable. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using over-the-counter medications. Its onset of action is typically 15 to 30 minutes, and it is poorly absorbed. This product is for rectal use only. Insert one suppository well into the rectum and retain it for 15 minutes; it does not need to melt completely to produce a laxative effect. Do not exceed one suppository daily unless directed by a doctor. For children aged 2 to under 6 years, use child-specific suppositories. For children under 2 years, consult a doctor.
